reference_assessment.trigger: User supplied MiGiC Poly, DirektDSP Polygraph and sgm-audio/guitar-mpe-transducer as possible accelerators.

migic_poly.published: Vendor advertises six independent voices, per-note pitch tracking, standard guitar input and ultra-low latency. Tracking engine is proprietary. Poly page gives no measured numerical chord-latency benchmark.
migic_poly.use: Behavioral reference for playable ordinary chords. Neural amp modelling does not establish how the pitch tracker is implemented. No reusable detector source identified.

polygraph.published: Vendor documents approximately 70 ms fixed lookahead, chord MIDI without pitch bend, and monophonic Lead mode with MPE. DAW compensation aligns recording but does not remove live monitoring delay. Re-plucks use note-off then note-on.
polygraph.use: Concrete comparison of ordinary chord tracking, re-pluck behavior and the quality/latency tradeoff; no published tracker implementation identified.

guitar_mpe_transducer.license: MIT source; C++20 with CLAP SDK and Catch2. No trained model or weights found.
guitar_mpe_transducer.implemented_scope: Mono audio YIN tracker with one active key/note ID. Fixed 2048-sample ring, pitch update every 64 samples; no demonstrated polyphonic pitch separation or physical-string inference.
guitar_mpe_transducer.use: Fixed-stack, sample-offset CLAP note/expression emitter is a possible future output-adapter reference. It is not a replacement for the current polyphonic detector or the immediate M3 bottleneck.
guitar_mpe_transducer.limits: Synthetic tone tests do not establish recorded-guitar behavior or M3 timing/allocation gates. Source review found onset/repluck synchronization and UMP note-off limitations; no code imported.
